newsitem.title: FRANCE: Left leads in French election seat projections.
newsitem.headline: Left leads in French election seat projections.

text.p: The combined left was ahead in the first projections for seats in the National Assembly released after the first round of voting in France's election on Sunday.
The BVA institute gave the ruling centre-right RPR/UDF coalition 255-275 seats, the Socialist party 250-270 seats, the Communist party 15-20 seats and the extreme right National Front 0-2 seats.
The Sofres polling institute gave the Socialist party 242-272 seats, the Communist party 21-30 seats, the RPR/UDF coalition 255-287 seats and the National Front 0-3 seats.
The final number of seats depends on a second round of voting set for June 1 in those constituencies where no single candidate polled more than 50 percent in Sunday's first round.
Centre-right parties had an overwhelming majority in the last National Assembly, which President Jacques Chirac dissolved almost a year ahead of schedule on April 21.
